headline: High: TREK’s browser/MCP and secret-handling surface can amplify Airbyte-fed data into leakage, conflicts, and compliance risk; prompt-injection is lower because no direct shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented, but TREK uses browsers and MCP while Airbyte can move data via APIs and broad egress. That makes manual or indirect content bridging plausible, yet the pair lacks evidence of default parser trust or filesystem coupling. Uncertainty keeps this above none but below medium.
conditions: IF Airbyte output is copied into TREK prompts or MCP inputs
IF both agents are connected through a shared clipboard, file drop, or message queue
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of raw upstream outputs into TREK
Route Airbyte outputs through a review step before MCP use
Separate workspaces and clipboards for the two agents
Add prompt-injection scanning to any shared handoff
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent content

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK explicitly touches API keys, MFA secrets, reservations, and documents, and it writes local files/logs. Airbyte has broad network egress and handles business data. If Airbyte ingests or exports TREK-held secrets or documents, the pair can exfiltrate sensitive data by default pathways; the evidence is indirect but sufficient to choose high over medium.
conditions: IF TREK data classes are synced into Airbyte connectors
IF Airbyte destinations include third-party services or logs
IF TREK uploads secrets or documents into shared storage
mitigations: Exclude secrets and MFA material from any Airbyte source
Restrict Airbyte destinations to approved internal systems
Move TREK uploads and logs to a separate volume
Rotate any exposed API keys or MFA secrets
requires-engineering: enforce field-level redaction on shared datasets

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte has broad network egress and API access, while TREK supports real-time collaborative sessions, multiple instances, and file-backed state. Even without explicit same-directory writes, overlapping mutable resources and concurrent sessions create a plausible conflict path. The lack of locking evidence pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same downstream API or database
IF TREK multiple instances operate on the same travel.db or uploads path
IF Airbyte sync jobs and TREK edits run concurrently
mitigations: Assign separate destinations or schemas per agent
Pause sync jobs during TREK write windows
Use file locks or transactional writes on shared state
Limit TREK instances touching the same workspace
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in, so it may act on upstream content; Airbyte can supply business data through APIs and broad egress. If Airbyte-fed records are treated as authoritative inside TREK, errors can cascade into plans, reservations, or budgets. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF Airbyte outputs are ingested into TREK without validation
IF TREK uses imported records to generate reservations or budgets
IF downstream actions are triggered from AI-generated summaries
mitigations: Require human review before TREK acts on imported data
Validate imported records against source systems
Mark Airbyte-fed fields as untrusted in TREK
Log and diff all AI-generated changes
requires-engineering: add source-of-truth checks before actions

E_compliance.rationale: TREK handles country visit history, reservations, documents, and secrets, while Airbyte handles business data and broad egress. If regulated or residency-sensitive travel data is moved through Airbyte, retention and residency controls may diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF TREK stores EU PII or travel documents in Airbyte-managed pipelines
IF Airbyte retention exceeds TREK deletion expectations
IF regulated data is exported to non-approved destinations
mitigations: Classify travel data before syncing it
Block regulated fields from Airbyte connectors
Align retention settings across both systems
Document residency for every destination
requires-engineering: implement deletion/export workflows end-to-end
